label: NOTE: what this set reaches, and what only the transcript run can
why: V92setParamsInfoFromCPUnPck and t_v92unpck.c were written by one hand from one reading of .text+0x12f00, so a green run says the two agree and not that either is right. Every entry below is a claim the disassembly makes: which source offset feeds which destination offset, which of the three flags gates which half, both clamp ceilings and the UNSIGNEDNESS of both clamps, the two filter scale factors and which arrays get which, and the single rounding of the gain. THE LAST ONE IS ONLY KILLABLE AT LEVEL 0 BY AN ARITHMETIC DIFFERENCE OF ONE ULP -- it was a live defect for one build and the block comparison caught it, which is why the fixture compares the block byte for byte rather than field by field. Entries that only change a format string are killable only by the level-2 transcript run; that is deliberate, since half this function is unreachable without it (finding 3544).

label: the drn print says the upstream rate is per drn and not per drn+17
the gain print loses its sign character
zero prints as positive
the fraction is scaled for %05d and not %06d
the whole part keeps its sign
why: EQUIVALENT BY PROOF, and the proof is the type of the source field. `gain` is `cp->prefilterGain * 2^-18 * 4000`; `prefilterGain` is UNSIGNED -- the object loads it with an explicitly zeroed high half and `fildll`, which is the unsigned conversion and not the signed one -- and both constants are positive. So `gain` is never negative, `(int)gain` and `(int)fabsf(gain)` agree over every value it can hold, and no fixture can separate them through THIS function. The sibling in V92Transmitter::reset is a different matter and is killed there, because the coefficients it prints are signed. Its two neighbours here -- the sign character and `sign_of`'s boundary -- ARE killable and are killed, by a case that forces prefilterGain to zero: zero is the one non-positive value gain can take, and the object prints it as '-'.
